## 9. QUALITY CONTROL – ROLL STOCK

### 9.1 Sampling procedure – incoming rolls

Sampling is carried out on receipt, before the delivery is booked into the
warehouse. The following applies to RS-52A and any other roll stock
currently in use.

For deliveries of up to 20 reels, inspect every reel. For deliveries of
21 to 100 reels, inspect a minimum of 10 reels selected at random from
different positions on the lorry (front, middle, rear, top and bottom
layers). For deliveries above 100 reels, inspect a minimum of 15 reels.
Record the results on the GRN and on the incoming inspection sheet
(QC-RS-01).

If any inspected reel fails a check, quarantine the entire delivery and
notify procurement. Do not part-use a delivery while a dispute is open
with the supplier.

### 9.2 Checks performed

Each sampled reel is checked for the following:

| Check | Method | Acceptance criterion |
|-------|--------|----------------------|
| Roll width | Steel tape, measured at three points around the circumference | 1,400 mm ± 3 mm |
| Outer diameter | Ultrasonic gauge or calibrated wrap | 1,250 mm ± 10 mm |
| Core diameter | Internal calliper | 100 mm ± 2 mm |
| Unit weight | Weighbridge or calibrated scale | 620 kg ± 15 kg |
| Core condition | Visual | No crush, no ovality, no protruding nails |
| Wound tension | Finger press on outer layer | No soft spots, no telescoping |
| Edge condition | Visual along both edges | No tears, no creases, no feathering |
| Moisture | Handheld moisture meter, three readings per roll | 6–8 % |
| Wrap/banding | Visual | Intact, no water staining |

### 9.3 Moisture measurement

Use the handheld moisture meter (model: Protimeter Mini, serial
M-2214). Take three readings per roll: one near the outer wrap, one at
mid-radius, and one at the core. Average the three readings. If the
average is outside 6–8 %, quarantine the roll and inform the warehouse
supervisor. Do not attempt to dry rolls on site.

### 9.4 Acceptance criteria – RS-52A

A delivery is accepted if:

- All sampled reels meet the checks in section 9.2.
- No more than one sampled reel shows a minor edge nick of less than
  5 mm depth, and that nick is on the outer 10 mm of the roll.
- The moisture average is within 6–8 % for every sampled reel.
- The supplier's delivery note matches the quantity and item code on
  the purchase order.

If a sampled reel shows telescoping of more than 5 mm, the whole
delivery is rejected. Do not attempt to re-band or re-wrap a telescoped
roll.

### 9.5 Rejected deliveries

When a delivery is rejected, the following applies:

1. Mark the GRN "REJECTED – see QC-RS-01" in red.
2. Photograph the defect on at least two reels.
3. Keep the delivery in the quarantine bay (bay 4) with a hold label.
4. Email procurement with the delivery note number, supplier, item
   code, quantity, and reason for rejection.
5. Do not return the goods to the supplier until a returns number has
   been issued.

Rejected rolls are not to be used for any edition, including the
weekend edition, without written authorisation from the production
manager.

### 9.6 In-use checks

Rolls are also checked when they are loaded onto the press. The press
crew should look for:

- Edge damage caused by forklift tines
- Loose outer wraps
- Core damage after removal from the reel stand
- Any sign of moisture staining on the outer layer

If a defect is found at the press, the roll is removed and set aside.
The press crew notes the reel number and the defect on the press log.
Warehouse staff collect the roll at the end of the shift and place it
in the quarantine bay. QC re-inspects the roll and, if it is usable,
it is returned to stock with a "RE-CHECKED" label. If it is not
usable, it is written off and the write-off form (WR-03) is completed.

Cumbria Ink Supplies – Product Data Sheet

Author: Technical Department, Cumbria Ink Supplies, Penrith Works, CA11 0AA

This sheet provides technical data for ink products supplied to the Herald group and other
commercial print customers. It is current as of the issue date above. Any revision that
supersedes this sheet will be circulated by email to the registered procurement contact and
posted to the supplier portal. Product codes are unchanged between revisions unless stated.

1. PRODUCT CODES AND NOMENCLATURE

All products are identified by a five-character code beginning with "CI". The code is printed
on the drum label, the delivery note, and the safety data sheet (SDS). When ordering, quote
the product code and the container size. A list of current codes follows.

| Product code | Product name | Container size | Colour |
|--------------|--------------|----------------|--------|
| CI-BLK-20 | Black ink 20L drum | 20 L | Black |
| CI-BLK-05 | Black ink 5L jerrycan | 5 L | Black |
| CI-CYN-20 | Cyan ink 20L drum | 20 L | Cyan |
| CI-MAG-20 | Magenta ink 20L drum | 20 L | Magenta |
| CI-YEL-20 | Yellow ink 20L drum | 20 L | Yellow |
| CI-CLN-01 | Wash-up solution 5L | 5 L | Clear |
| CI-FIN-01 | Fountain solution concentrate 1L | 1 L | Clear |

2. BLACK INK – CI-BLK-20 (CURRENT)

2.1 Description
High-density, fast-setting black ink for coldset web offset printing on newsprint. Suitable
for the Herald press run and comparable regional titles. Formulated for consistent
density across a range of press speeds.

2.2 Container and volume
Container type: cylindrical drum with removable lid, fitted with a 55 mm bung.
Nominal fill volume: Black ink 20L drum unit_volume_litres_per_drum 20 L. Record status: current.
This is the fill volume at 20 °C. Do not rely on visual level in the drum; use the
calibrated dipstick supplied with each pallet if a check is required.

2.3 Physical properties (at 20 °C unless stated)
- Density: 1.06 g/cm³
- Viscosity (Brookfield, spindle 3, 20 rpm): 2.4 Pa·s
- Fineness of grind (Hegman gauge): 7.5
- Flash point: > 100 °C (closed cup)
- Drying time on newsprint (23 °C, 50 % RH): < 90 seconds

2.4 Colour and strength
Blackness (density at 1.0 film thickness): 1.75 ± 0.05
Tinting strength: 100 ± 3 relative to reference standard.

2.6 Storage conditions
Store in original sealed drums between 5 °C and 30 °C. Avoid direct sunlight and frost.
Keep away from oxidising agents and foodstuffs. Shelf life from date of manufacture:
24 months in unopened drum. Once opened, use within 6 months and keep the lid
closed when not in use. Do not store near heat sources or open flames.

2.7 Handling and disposal
Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses when handling. Wash skin with soap and water
after contact. Spillages: absorb with inert material (e.g. sand or proprietary spill kit),
place in a labelled waste container. Dispose of waste ink and contaminated packaging in
accordance with local environmental regulations. Do not pour down drains.

3. PROCESS COLOUR INKS – CI-CYN-20, CI-MAG-20, CI-YEL-20 (CURRENT)

3.1 Description
Process colour inks for four-colour coldset printing. Supplied in 20 L drums. These
products are matched to the ISO 2846-1 colour standard for newsprint inks.
3.2 Container and volume

Container type: cylindrical drum with removable lid, fitted with a 55 mm bung.
Nominal fill volume: Cyan ink 20L drum unit_volume_litres_per_drum 20 L. Record status: current.
This is the fill volume at 20 °C. Do not rely on visual level in the drum; use the
calibrated dipstick supplied with each pallet if a check is required.

3.3 Physical properties (at 20 °C unless stated)

Cyan ink CI-CYN-20:
- Density: 1.04 g/cm³
- Viscosity (Brookfield, spindle 3, 20 rpm): 2.2 Pa·s
- Fineness of grind (Hegman gauge): 7.5
- Flash point: > 100 °C (closed cup)
- Drying time on newsprint (23 °C, 50 % RH): < 90 seconds

Magenta ink CI-MAG-20:
- Density: 1.05 g/cm³
- Viscosity (Brookfield, spindle 3, 20 rpm): 2.3 Pa·s
- Fineness of grind (Hegman gauge): 7.5
- Flash point: > 100 °C (closed cup)
- Drying time on newsprint (23 °C, 50 % RH): < 90 seconds

Yellow ink CI-YEL-20:
- Density: 1.03 g/cm³
- Viscosity (Brookfield, spindle 3, 20 rpm): 2.1 Pa·s
- Fineness of grind (Hegman gauge): 7.5
- Flash point: > 100 °C (closed cup)
- Drying time on newsprint (23 °C, 50 % RH): < 90 seconds

3.4 Colour and strength

Cyan (CI-CYN-20):
- Colour strength: 100 ± 3 relative to reference standard.
- Hue angle (CIELAB, D50/2°): 223° ± 2°
- Chroma: 72 ± 2

Magenta (CI-MAG-20):
- Colour strength: 100 ± 3 relative to reference standard.
- Hue angle (CIELAB, D50/2°): 343° ± 2°
- Chroma: 74 ± 2

Yellow (CI-YEL-20):
- Colour strength: 100 ± 3 relative to reference standard.
- Hue angle (CIELAB, D50/2°): 92° ± 2°
- Chroma: 88 ± 2

3.5 Drying and setting notes

3.6 Colour matching and batch consistency

Each batch is tested against the reference standard supplied by Cumbria Ink
Supplies. A colour match certificate is available on request for each batch
number. If a colour difference is suspected, contact the technical helpline
before adjusting the press. Do not mix inks from different batches without
checking compatibility; minor batch-to-batch variation is normal and within the
tolerances stated above.

For four-colour work, the recommended printing sequence is black, cyan, magenta,
yellow. This sequence gives the best trapping and reduces the risk of set-off
on the folder.

3.7 Storage conditions

Store in original sealed drums between 5 °C and 30 °C. Avoid direct sunlight and
frost. Keep away from oxidising agents and foodstuffs. Shelf life from date of
manufacture: 24 months in unopened drum. Once opened, use within 6 months and
keep the lid closed when not in use. Do not store near heat sources or open
flames.

3.8 Handling and disposal

Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses when handling. Wash skin with soap and
water after contact. Spillages: absorb with inert material (e.g. sand or
proprietary spill kit), place in a labelled waste container. Dispose of waste ink
and contaminated packaging in accordance with local environmental regulations.
Do not pour down drains.

3.9 Safety data

Refer to the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for each product before use. SDS documents
are supplied with the first delivery of each batch and are available on request
from Cumbria Ink Supplies. Keep SDS documents accessible to all pressroom staff.

4. SPECIALITY INKS – CI-UV-CLR-20, CI-UV-BLK-20 (CURRENT)

4.1 Description

UV-curable inks for occasional use on coated stock or for covers that require a
gloss finish. These inks are not for routine newsprint use; they require a UV
lamp unit fitted to the press. The Herald printworks currently has one UV unit
available for the weekend edition cover.
4.2 Product data

| Property | CI-UV-CLR-20 | CI-UV-BLK-20 |
|---|---|---|
| Colour | Clear gloss | Black |
| Viscosity at 25 °C (Brookfield, spindle 4, 20 rpm) | 2.8–3.4 Pa·s | 3.0–3.6 Pa·s |
| Density at 20 °C | 1.05–1.10 g/cm³ | 1.08–1.13 g/cm³ |
| Cure speed (typical, 120 W/cm medium-pressure mercury lamp) | 12–18 m/min | 10–15 m/min |
| Fineness of grind (Hegman) | — | ≥ 7 |
| Substrate | Coated stock, board | Coated stock, board |
| Finish | Gloss | Gloss |
| Lightfastness | Not rated for outdoor use | Not rated for outdoor use |

4.3 Handling and disposal

UV inks are not classified as hazardous waste under current regulations, but
they must not be discharged to drains or watercourses. Uncured UV ink is an
irritant; avoid skin contact. Wear nitrile gloves, safety glasses and a
suitable apron when handling. If ink comes into contact with skin, wipe off
with a dry cloth before washing with soap and water; do not use solvents to
clean skin.

Spillages of uncured ink: absorb with inert granules or a proprietary spill
kit, then sweep into a labelled waste container. Cured ink residue may be
removed with a scraper and disposed of with general non-hazardous waste where
local rules permit. Contaminated rags and wipes should be placed in a sealed
metal bin and disposed of as special waste.

4.4 Shelf life and storage

Store UV inks in original sealed containers between 10 °C and 25 °C. Do not
expose to direct sunlight or strong artificial light, as this may cause
premature curing in the container. Shelf life from date of manufacture:
12 months in unopened container. Once opened, use within 3 months and keep
the lid tightly closed when not in use. Do not return unused ink to the
original container.

4.5 Batch numbering

All Cumbria Ink Supplies products carry a batch number printed on the drum
label. The format is YYMMDD-LLL-NNN, where YYMMDD is the date of manufacture,
LLL is the production line code (CLR or BLK for these products), and NNN is a
sequential number. For example, batch 260813-CLR-014 was manufactured on
13 August 2026 on the clear line. Please quote the full batch number in all
correspondence, including colour match certificate requests and any
complaints.

4.6 Safety data

Refer to the Safety Data Sheet (SDS) for CI-UV-CLR-20 and CI-UV-BLK-20 before
use. SDS documents are supplied with the first delivery of each batch and are
available on request from Cumbria Ink Supplies. Keep SDS documents accessible
to all pressroom staff.

4.7 Compatibility note

UV inks should not be mixed with conventional news inks or with the CI-NEWS
range. If a press is changed over from conventional to UV ink, the inking
system and rollers must be cleaned thoroughly first. Contact the technical
helpline for a recommended cleaning procedure. UV inks are formulated for use
with the current UV lamp unit at the Herald printworks; if a different lamp
unit is fitted, re-test cure speed before full production.

5. ORDERING INFORMATION

5.1 Product codes

| Product code | Description | Pack size |
|---|---|---|
| CI-NEWS-BLK-20 | Black news ink, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |
| CI-NEWS-CYN-20 | Cyan news ink, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |
| CI-NEWS-MGN-20 | Magenta news ink, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |
| CI-NEWS-YEL-20 | Yellow news ink, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |
| CI-UV-CLR-20 | UV clear gloss, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |
| CI-UV-BLK-20 | UV black, 20 kg drum | 20 kg |

5.2 Minimum order quantities

Minimum order is one full drum of any product code. Part drums are not
supplied. Orders for four-colour sets (one drum of each of the four CI-NEWS
codes) are delivered on a shared pallet. A delivery note and colour match
certificate accompany every order.
5.3 Ordering procedure

Orders may be placed by telephone, email, or fax. The Herald printworks
normally orders by email to orders@cumbriaink.co.uk with the subject line
"INK ORDER" followed by the date. Please include the following in every
order:

- Product code and quantity (in whole drums)
- Delivery address and any access instructions for the loading bay
- Required delivery date
- Purchase order number, if applicable
- Contact name and telephone number for delivery queries

Orders received before 12:00 on a working day are normally dispatched the
following working day. Orders received after 12:00 may be delayed by one
working day. Deliveries are made Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00, excluding
public holidays. The Herald printworks is normally closed on bank holidays,
so deliveries scheduled for a bank holiday will be moved to the next working
day unless the customer requests otherwise.

5.4 Delivery and returns

All deliveries are made on a pallet base. Drums are shrink-wrapped and
labelled with the product code, batch number, and a handling label. Please
inspect the delivery note against the goods received before signing.
Shortages or damage must be reported to Cumbria Ink Supplies within 48 hours
of delivery. Claims received after 48 hours cannot be accepted unless the
damage is hidden and is reported within 5 working days of discovery.

If a drum is received damaged or leaking, do not open it. Keep the drum
upright and isolate it from other materials. Contact the technical helpline
immediately for disposal instructions. Do not return damaged drums without
prior agreement from Cumbria Ink Supplies.

Returns of unopened, undamaged drums are accepted within 14 days of delivery
for credit, subject to a 25 per cent restocking charge. Returned drums must
be in their original packaging with the original labels intact. The customer
pays the cost of return carriage. No returns are accepted for opened drums
or for inks that have been mixed with other products.

5.5 Pricing and payment

Prices are quoted per drum and are exclusive of VAT and delivery charges.
Prices are confirmed at the time of order and are held for 30 days from the
date of quotation. The Herald printworks is invoiced on a monthly account
with payment terms of 30 days net from the date of invoice. Invoices are
sent by email unless a paper copy is requested.

5.6 Technical helpline

The technical helpline is available Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00, on
01768 555 014. Calls outside these hours are answered by an answering
service; messages are returned on the next working day. The helpline can
assist with:

- Cure speed testing and lamp unit settings
- Cleaning procedures for press changeovers
- Colour matching and colour match certificates
- Ink viscosity and pressroom temperature issues
- Disposal of unused or out-of-date ink

Please have the batch number and product code ready when calling. The
helpline team will ask for these details to identify the exact formulation.

6. STORAGE AND SHELF LIFE

6.1 Storage conditions

Store drums upright in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area. Avoid direct
sunlight and keep away from sources of heat, including radiators, steam
pipes, and hot press parts. The recommended storage temperature is 10 to
25°C. Drums should not be stacked more than two high. If drums are stacked,
place a slip sheet between layers to prevent the labels from being damaged.

Keep the drum lid tightly closed when not in use. Do not transfer ink to an
unlabelled container. Partly used drums should be stored with the original
label facing outward so the batch number remains visible.

## 9. QUALITY CONTROL – ROLL STOCK

### 9.1 Sampling procedure – incoming rolls

Sampling is carried out on receipt, before the delivery is booked into the
warehouse. The following applies to RS-52A and any other roll stock
currently in use.

For deliveries of up to 20 reels, inspect every reel. For deliveries of
21 to 100 reels, inspect a minimum of 10 reels selected at random from
different positions on the lorry (front, middle, rear, top and bottom
layers). For deliveries above 100 reels, inspect a minimum of 15 reels.
Record the results on the GRN and on the incoming inspection sheet
(QC-RS-01).

If any inspected reel fails a check, quarantine the entire delivery and
notify procurement. Do not part-use a delivery while a dispute is open
with the supplier.

### 9.2 Checks performed

Each sampled reel is checked for the following:

| Check | Method | Acceptance criterion |
|-------|--------|----------------------|
| Roll width | Steel tape, measured at three points around the circumference | 1,400 mm ± 3 mm |
| Outer diameter | Ultrasonic gauge or calibrated wrap | 1,250 mm ± 10 mm |
| Core diameter | Internal calliper | 100 mm ± 2 mm |
| Unit weight | Weighbridge or calibrated scale | 620 kg ± 15 kg |
| Core condition | Visual | No crush, no ovality, no protruding nails |
| Wound tension | Finger press on outer layer | No soft spots, no telescoping |
| Edge condition | Visual along both edges | No tears, no creases, no feathering |
| Moisture | Handheld moisture meter, three readings per roll | 6–8 % |
| Wrap/banding | Visual | Intact, no water staining |

### 9.3 Moisture measurement

Use the handheld moisture meter (model: Protimeter Mini, serial
M-2214). Take three readings per roll: one near the outer wrap, one at
mid-radius, and one at the core. Average the three readings. If the
average is outside 6–8 %, quarantine the roll and inform the warehouse
supervisor. Do not attempt to dry rolls on site.

### 9.4 Acceptance criteria – RS-52A

A delivery is accepted if:

- All sampled reels meet the checks in section 9.2.
- No more than one sampled reel shows a minor edge nick of less than
  5 mm depth, and that nick is on the outer 10 mm of the roll.
- The moisture average is within 6–8 % for every sampled reel.
- The supplier's delivery note matches the quantity and item code on
  the purchase order.

If a sampled reel shows telescoping of more than 5 mm, the whole
delivery is rejected. Do not attempt to re-band or re-wrap a telescoped
roll.

### 9.5 Rejected deliveries

When a delivery is rejected, the following applies:

1. Mark the GRN "REJECTED – see QC-RS-01" in red.
2. Photograph the defect on at least two reels.
3. Keep the delivery in the quarantine bay (bay 4) with a hold label.
4. Email procurement with the delivery note number, supplier, item
   code, quantity, and reason for rejection.
5. Do not return the goods to the supplier until a returns number has
   been issued.

Rejected rolls are not to be used for any edition, including the
weekend edition, without written authorisation from the production
manager.

### 9.6 In-use checks

Rolls are also checked when they are loaded onto the press. The press
crew should look for:

- Edge damage caused by forklift tines
- Loose outer wraps
- Core damage after removal from the reel stand
- Any sign of moisture staining on the outer layer

If a defect is found at the press, the roll is removed and set aside.
The press crew notes the reel number and the defect on the press log.
Warehouse staff collect the roll at the end of the shift and place it
in the quarantine bay. QC re-inspects the roll and, if it is usable,
it is returned to stock with a "RE-CHECKED" label. If it is not
usable, it is written off and the write-off form (WR-03) is completed.

Cumbria Ink Supplies – Product Data Sheet
Product Data Sheet: PDS-CIS-2026-04 (Revision 3, current)
Issued: 11 August 2026

Author: Technical Department, Cumbria Ink Supplies, Penrith Works, CA11 0AA
Telephone: 01768 899 214 (option 2, Technical)
Email: tech.enquiries@cumbriaink.co.uk

This sheet provides technical data for ink products supplied to the Herald group and other
commercial print customers. It is current as of the issue date above. Any revision that
supersedes this sheet will be circulated by email to the registered procurement contact and
posted to the supplier portal. Product codes are unchanged between revisions unless stated.

1. PRODUCT CODES AND NOMENCLATURE

All products are identified by a five-character code beginning with "CI". The code is printed
on the drum label, the delivery note, and the safety data sheet (SDS). When ordering, quote
the product code and the container size. A list of current codes follows.

| Product code | Product name | Container size | Colour |
|--------------|--------------|----------------|--------|
| CI-BLK-20 | Black ink 20L drum | 20 L | Black |
| CI-BLK-05 | Black ink 5L jerrycan | 5 L | Black |

| CI-MAG-20 | Magenta ink 20L drum | 20 L | Magenta |
| CI-YEL-20 | Yellow ink 20L drum | 20 L | Yellow |
| CI-CLN-01 | Wash-up solution 5L | 5 L | Clear |
| CI-FIN-01 | Fountain solution concentrate 1L | 1 L | Clear |

2. BLACK INK – CI-BLK-20 (CURRENT)

2.1 Description
High-density, fast-setting black ink for coldset web offset printing on newsprint. Suitable
for the Herald press run and comparable regional titles. Formulated for consistent
density across a range of press speeds.

2.2 Container and volume
Container type: cylindrical drum with removable lid, fitted with a 55 mm bung.
Nominal fill volume: Black ink 20L drum unit_volume_litres_per_drum 20 L. Record status: current.
This is the fill volume at 20 °C. Do not rely on visual level in the drum; use the
calibrated dipstick supplied with each pallet if a check is required.

2.3 Physical properties (at 20 °C unless stated)
- Density: 1.06 g/cm³
- Viscosity (Brookfield, spindle 3, 20 rpm): 2.4 Pa·s
- Fineness of grind (Hegman gauge): 7.5
- Flash point: > 100 °C (closed cup)
- Drying time on newsprint (23 °C, 50 % RH): < 90 seconds

2.4 Colour and strength
Blackness (density at 1.0 film thickness): 1.75 ± 0.05
Tinting strength: 100 ± 3 relative to reference standard.

2.6 Storage conditions
Store in original sealed drums between 5 °C and 30 °C. Avoid direct sunlight and frost.
Keep away from oxidising agents and foodstuffs. Shelf life from date of manufacture:
24 months in unopened drum. Once opened, use within 6 months and keep the lid
closed when not in use. Do not store near heat sources or open flames.

2.7 Handling and disposal
Wear nitrile gloves and safety glasses when handling. Wash skin with soap and water
after contact. Spillages: absorb with inert material (e.g. sand or proprietary spill kit),
place in a labelled waste container. Dispose of waste ink and contaminated packaging in
accordance with local environmental regulations. Do not pour down drains.

3. PROCESS COLOUR INKS – CI-CYN-20, CI-MAG-20, CI-YEL-20 (CURRENT)

3.1 Description
Process colour inks for four-colour coldset printing. Supplied in 20 L drums. These
products are matched to the ISO 2846-1 colour standard for newsprint inks.

3.5 Drying and setting notes

3.6 Colour matching and batch consistency

Each batch is tested against the reference standard supplied by Cumbria Ink
Supplies. A colour match certificate is available on request for each batch

before adjusting the press. Do not mix inks from different batches without
checking compatibility; minor batch-to-batch variation is normal and within the
tolerances stated above.

For four-colour work, the recommended printing sequence is black, cyan, magenta,
yellow. This sequence gives the best trapping and reduces the risk of set-off
on the folder.

3.7 Storage conditions

3.9 Safety data

4. SPECIALITY INKS – CI-UV-CLR-20, CI-UV-BLK-20 (CURRENT)

4.3 Handling and disposal

UV inks are not classified as hazardous waste under current regulations, but
they must not be discharged to drains or watercourses. Uncured UV ink is an
irritant; avoid skin contact. Wear nitrile gloves, safety glasses and a
suitable apron when handling. If ink comes into contact with skin, wipe off
with a dry cloth before washing with soap and water; do not use solvents to
clean skin.

Spillages of uncured ink: absorb with inert granules or a proprietary spill
kit, then sweep into a labelled waste container. Cured ink residue may be
removed with a scraper and disposed of with general non-hazardous waste where
local rules permit. Contaminated rags and wipes should be placed in a sealed
metal bin and disposed of as special waste.

4.4 Shelf life and storage

Store UV inks in original sealed containers between 10 °C and 25 °C. Do not
expose to direct sunlight or strong artificial light, as this may cause
premature curing in the container. Shelf life from date of manufacture:
12 months in unopened container. Once opened, use within 3 months and keep
the lid tightly closed when not in use. Do not return unused ink to the
original container.

4.5 Batch numbering

All Cumbria Ink Supplies products carry a batch number printed on the drum
label. The format is YYMMDD-LLL-NNN, where YYMMDD is the date of manufacture,
LLL is the production line code (CLR or BLK for these products), and NNN is a
sequential number. For example, batch 260813-CLR-014 was manufactured on
13 August 2026 on the clear line. Please quote the full batch number in all
correspondence, including colour match certificate requests and any
complaints.

use. SDS documents are supplied with the first delivery of each batch and are
available on request from Cumbria Ink Supplies. Keep SDS documents accessible
to all pressroom staff.

4.7 Compatibility note

UV inks should not be mixed with conventional news inks or with the CI-NEWS
range. If a press is changed over from conventional to UV ink, the inking
system and rollers must be cleaned thoroughly first. Contact the technical
helpline for a recommended cleaning procedure. UV inks are formulated for use
with the current UV lamp unit at the Herald printworks; if a different lamp
unit is fitted, re-test cure speed before full production.

5.3 Ordering procedure

Orders may be placed by telephone, email, or fax. The Herald printworks
normally orders by email to orders@cumbriaink.co.uk with the subject line
"INK ORDER" followed by the date. Please include the following in every
order:

- Product code and quantity (in whole drums)
- Delivery address and any access instructions for the loading bay
- Required delivery date
- Purchase order number, if applicable
- Contact name and telephone number for delivery queries

Orders received before 12:00 on a working day are normally dispatched the
following working day. Orders received after 12:00 may be delayed by one
working day. Deliveries are made Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 17:00, excluding
public holidays. The Herald printworks is normally closed on bank holidays,
so deliveries scheduled for a bank holiday will be moved to the next working
day unless the customer requests otherwise.

5.4 Delivery and returns

All deliveries are made on a pallet base. Drums are shrink-wrapped and
labelled with the product code, batch number, and a handling label. Please
inspect the delivery note against the goods received before signing.
Shortages or damage must be reported to Cumbria Ink Supplies within 48 hours
of delivery. Claims received after 48 hours cannot be accepted unless the
damage is hidden and is reported within 5 working days of discovery.

If a drum is received damaged or leaking, do not open it. Keep the drum
upright and isolate it from other materials. Contact the technical helpline
immediately for disposal instructions. Do not return damaged drums without
prior agreement from Cumbria Ink Supplies.

Returns of unopened, undamaged drums are accepted within 14 days of delivery
for credit, subject to a 25 per cent restocking charge. Returned drums must
be in their original packaging with the original labels intact. The customer
pays the cost of return carriage. No returns are accepted for opened drums
or for inks that have been mixed with other products.

5.5 Pricing and payment

Prices are quoted per drum and are exclusive of VAT and delivery charges.
Prices are confirmed at the time of order and are held for 30 days from the
date of quotation. The Herald printworks is invoiced on a monthly account
with payment terms of 30 days net from the date of invoice. Invoices are
sent by email unless a paper copy is requested.

5.6 Technical helpline

The technical helpline is available Monday to Friday, 08:30 to 17:00, on
01768 555 014. Calls outside these hours are answered by an answering
service; messages are returned on the next working day. The helpline can
assist with:

- Cure speed testing and lamp unit settings
- Cleaning procedures for press changeovers
- Colour matching and colour match certificates
- Ink viscosity and pressroom temperature issues
- Disposal of unused or out-of-date ink

Please have the batch number and product code ready when calling. The
helpline team will ask for these details to identify the exact formulation.

6. STORAGE AND SHELF LIFE

6.1 Storage conditions

Store drums upright in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area. Avoid direct
sunlight and keep away from sources of heat, including radiators, steam
pipes, and hot press parts. The recommended storage temperature is 10 to
25°C. Drums should not be stacked more than two high. If drums are stacked,
place a slip sheet between layers to prevent the labels from being damaged.

Keep the drum lid tightly closed when not in use. Do not transfer ink to an
unlabelled container. Partly used drums should be stored with the original
label facing outward so the batch number remains visible.
